liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Reviewer says the fifth tune of set one is Weather Report Suite, which the setlist doesn't annotate [16]
- **Dark Star v1** (1 review): Reviewer says the first verse was played acoustically, and the band then went electric for the second verse [7]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): Reviewer notes that Oteil sang the lead vocal on this song [12]
- **Chimenti solo** (1 review): Jeff's piano showcase after the Dark Star reprise led into Days Between, and the reviewer enjoyed it [12]
- **Days Between** (1 review): Reviewer says Bob has been owning this song lately [7]

## Setlist highlights

- **Candyman**: rare: 8 archived performances [19]
- **Dark Star v1**: rare: 12 archived performances [19]
- **Chimenti solo**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [19]

## The recordings

- **deadandcompany2017-06-18.akg414b-uls.sunboy.flac24** (recommended): source not stated; 19 songs; 164 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **deadandcompany2017-06-18.akg414b-uls.sunboy.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 164 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **dac2017-06-18.sennmke4010.mbhoka200n.tascamdr680.busmanmod.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 163 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]
- **DC2017-06-18.MG21**: source not stated; 17 songs; 162 min; rated 3.9/5 by 10 [4]
- **deadco2017-06-18.mbhoka200.flac24**: source not stated; 18 songs; 163 min [5]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended, standing in the pit about fifteen feet from the stage [9]
- John and Bob played acoustic guitars for part of the show; the lineup included Mickey, Bill, Oteil and Jeff [1]
- Reviewer says the band is comfortable and mixing things up the way the Dead did in the 1970s [7]
- Reviewer disputes that an acoustic Dark Star is historic for the Dead, saying it has been done before [11]
- Reviewer thinks the band has hit its stride since the Pennsylvania shows, and calls the two Boston shows outstanding [12]
- Reviewer heard the Salt Lake show too, found it good, and thinks the band improves each show, with this Fenway night standing out [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **deadandcompany2017-06-18.akg414b-uls.sunboy.flac24**: taped by Steven Weld; transferred by Steven Weld; source: 2 AKG c414b-uls'(hyper cardioid)>GAKables xlr(15')>Lunatec V2>GAKables xlr>Apogee Mini-Me@24/96>AES/EBU>Sound Devices 722 @24bit/96kHz [1]. Also: Taped on the turf in section C5, behind row nine in the taper's section left of the mixer enclosure; Two AKG c414b-uls hypercardioid mics on a stereo bar, on a tall stand at nine feet, aimed just outside the PA stacks [1]
- **deadandcompany2017-06-18.akg414b-uls.sunboy.flac16**: taped by Steven Weld; transferred by Steven Weld; source: 2 AKG c414b-uls'(hyper cardioid)>GAKables xlr(15')>Lunatec V2>GAKables xlr>Apogee Mini-Me@24/96>AES/EBU>Sound Devices 722 @24bit/96kHz [2]. Also: A source link to an etree database entry for this AKG 414 recording was added [18]
- **dac2017-06-18.sennmke4010.mbhoka200n.tascamdr680.busmanmod.flac16**: taped by Bob Crupi; transferred by Bob Crupi; source: Senn MS14P/mke4010 (cards/din) + MBHO603/ka200n (ortf) > Tascam DR-680 (Busman Mod) [3]. Also: Transfer went through Cakewalk Sonar mixdown and Sound Forge 11 with dither and resampling, then flac at level 8 with ffp [3]
- **DC2017-06-18.MG21**: taped by Keith Antaya; transferred by Keith Antaya; source: MG21>nbox>R44 [4]. Also: A source link was added to the page. The uploaded md5 files failed verification, so a new ffp file was made from the flacs [13]
- **deadco2017-06-18.mbhoka200.flac24**: taped by Bob Crupi; transferred by Bob Crupi; source: MBHO603/ka200n (ortf)->Tascam DR-680 (Busman Mod) [5]. Also: Bob Crupi recorded with MBHO603/ka200n ORTF into a modded Tascam DR-680, then transferred via Sound Forge 11 to flac [5]
